metadata.analyzed_by: AWS Transform Custom — Agentic Readiness Analysis
metadata.archetype_justification: Application reads shipping rates from MongoDB and performs arithmetic quote calculations. No write operations to persistent state. Primarily a read-only data access layer.

findings.title: Machine Identity Authentication
findings.description: The application uses a single static API key ('ship-2013-abc123-static') hardcoded in server.js. All callers share the same key with no principal attribution. No OAuth2, mTLS, Cognito, or machine identity mechanism exists.
findings.gap: No machine identity authentication. A single shared static key provides no caller attribution, no rotation capability, and no per-agent identity.
findings.recommendation: Implement API Gateway with IAM authorization or Cognito app client credentials flow. Each agent/caller gets a unique client ID logged with every request.

blocker_remediation.immediate: Implement API Gateway with IAM authorization or Cognito app client credentials flow in front of this service.
blocker_remediation.target_state: Each calling agent has a unique machine identity with principal attribution in access logs.

findings.title: Scoped Permissions (Least Privilege)
findings.description: The application has a single API key that grants full access to all endpoints. No mechanism to differentiate access levels — all callers get identical permissions.
findings.gap: No scoped permission model. Cannot grant read-only access to /rates without also granting access to /quote.
findings.recommendation: Introduce API Gateway with usage plans and per-consumer API keys, or implement Cognito with OAuth scopes mapped to endpoint access.

compensating_controls: Deploy API Gateway with separate API keys per consumer mapped to resource policies
Use IAM policies with method-level authorization at the API Gateway layer

findings.title: Action-Level Authorization
findings.description: No action-level authorization exists. The middleware only validates a single shared API key. No RBAC, ABAC, or permission differentiation between GET and POST operations.
findings.gap: Cannot restrict an agent to read-only operations while blocking computation operations within the same authentication context.
findings.recommendation: Implement method-level authorization at API Gateway or within application middleware.

compensating_controls: API Gateway method-level authorization with different IAM policies per HTTP method
Network-level restrictions limiting specific callers to specific paths

findings.title: Credential Management
findings.description: API key is hardcoded in source code (server.js line 9). MongoDB connection string with IP address is also hardcoded (line 12). K8s deployment references a Kubernetes secret, but application source still embeds credentials.
findings.gap: Credentials embedded in source code. No secrets management system. No rotation capability.
findings.recommendation: Remove hardcoded credentials. Read from environment variables. Integrate AWS Secrets Manager for credential storage and rotation.

compensating_controls: K8s deployment.yaml references shipping-rate-api-secret for API_KEY env var
Restrict repository access to limit credential exposure

findings.title: Immutable Audit Logging
findings.description: No audit logging exists. No logging middleware, no CloudTrail, no access logs. Only output is startup console.log. No request is logged with caller identity, timestamp, or action.
findings.gap: Zero audit trail. Cannot determine who called what endpoint, when, or with what parameters.
findings.recommendation: Add request logging middleware. Deploy behind API Gateway with access logging to CloudWatch. Enable S3 export with Object Lock for immutability.

ara_metadata.conditional_resolution: Resolved to RISK-SAFETY: agent_scope=read-only, audit logging still important but not a deployment blocker.
ara_metadata.resolution_reasoning: Read-only agents do not execute write operations, reducing the compliance risk of missing audit trails. Still a RISK-SAFETY because read operations on business data should be attributable.
compensating_controls: Deploy behind API Gateway with access logging enabled to CloudWatch
Add k8s-level request logging via service mesh sidecar

findings.title: Agent Identity Suspension
findings.description: Only one shared API key exists. Cannot be selectively revoked for a specific agent without affecting all callers. No mechanism to disable individual agent identities.
findings.gap: Cannot suspend a single misbehaving agent without revoking access for all consumers.
findings.recommendation: Implement per-agent API keys via API Gateway usage plans or per-agent Cognito app clients, each independently revocable.

compensating_controls: API Gateway with per-consumer API keys allows individual key deletion
Network-level blocking of specific caller IPs as emergency measure

findings.title: Rate Limiting and Throttling
findings.description: No rate limiting at any layer. No API Gateway, WAF, or ingress-level throttling configured. Express application has no rate-limiting middleware. K8s service is ClusterIP with no traffic management.
findings.gap: Unlimited request volume can overwhelm the application and backing MongoDB instance.
findings.recommendation: Add API Gateway with throttling configuration or implement application-level rate limiting via express-rate-limit.

compensating_controls: Add express-rate-limit middleware as application-level fix
Deploy Kubernetes ingress with rate-limiting annotations

findings.title: PII Redaction in Logs
findings.description: No PII redaction framework. MongoDB documents returned without field filtering via .find(filter).toArray(). No log scrubbing infrastructure exists.
findings.gap: No PII masking or field-level filtering on responses or logs. If rates collection contains sensitive fields, they are exposed.
findings.recommendation: Add field projection to MongoDB queries to return only needed fields. Implement PII redaction middleware when adding logging.

compensating_controls: Current lack of logging means PII is not actively leaking to logs today
Implement field projection in MongoDB queries

findings.title: Machine-Readable API Specification
findings.description: No OpenAPI, Swagger, AsyncAPI, GraphQL schema, or equivalent machine-readable specification exists in the repository.
findings.gap: Agent tool generation requires manual authoring that will drift from actual behavior.
findings.recommendation: Create an OpenAPI 3.0 specification documenting both endpoints (GET /rates and POST /quote) with request/response schemas.

compensating_controls: Manually author an OpenAPI spec based on the two endpoints
Use API Gateway import to generate a spec from route definitions

findings.title: Structured Error Responses
findings.description: Error responses are minimal ({ error: 'string' }) with HTTP status codes. No error code taxonomy, no retryable indicator, no structured error format.
findings.gap: Agents cannot distinguish retriable from terminal errors.
findings.recommendation: Implement structured error format: { error_code, message, retryable }. Map database errors to retriable and validation errors to non-retriable.

compensating_controls: Agent-side retry logic with exponential backoff on 5xx
API Gateway custom error responses

findings.title: Input Validation and Schema Enforcement
findings.description: No input validation exists. Query parameters (origin, dest) passed directly into MongoDB queries without validation. POST body fields (weight, zone) used in arithmetic without type checking.
findings.gap: Malformed agent inputs accepted without rejection. No structured validation error responses.
findings.recommendation: Add input validation middleware (joi, express-validator, or zod). Validate weight and zone as numeric. Validate origin and dest format. Return structured validation errors.

compensating_controls: API Gateway request validators with JSON Schema
MongoDB driver parameterization prevents injection

findings.title: Schema Versioning and API Contracts
findings.description: No API versioning. Endpoints are unversioned (/rates, /quote). No schema documentation, no changelog, no breaking change detection, no CI/CD.
findings.gap: API changes will break agent tool bindings silently. No mechanism to detect or communicate breaking changes.
findings.recommendation: Introduce URL path versioning (/v1/). Create OpenAPI spec as versioned contract. Add contract testing when CI is established.

compensating_controls: Pin agent tool definitions to specific response field expectations
Add URL path versioning as low-effort first step

findings.title: Distributed Tracing and Structured Logging
findings.description: No distributed tracing or structured logging exists. No OpenTelemetry, X-Ray, or tracing instrumentation. No JSON logging. No correlation IDs.
findings.gap: Agent-initiated requests cannot be traced through the system. Failures are invisible.
findings.recommendation: Add OpenTelemetry SDK for distributed tracing. Implement structured JSON logging with correlation IDs.

compensating_controls: API Gateway access logs provide basic request-level visibility
Kubernetes pod logs capture stdout

findings.title: Alerting on Error Rates and Latency
findings.description: No alerting configuration exists. No CloudWatch alarms, no PagerDuty/OpsGenie integration, no SLO definitions.
findings.gap: Service degradation affecting agent consumers will go undetected.
findings.recommendation: Define CloudWatch alarms for error rate (5xx >5%) and p99 latency (>2s). Integrate with notification channel.

compensating_controls: Kubernetes liveness/readiness probes provide basic availability detection
External synthetic monitoring

findings.title: Infrastructure Governance for Agent-Facing Surface
findings.description: K8s manifests exist but no IaC for API Gateway, IAM, secrets, or networking. No CI/CD for review enforcement. No drift detection.
findings.gap: Integration surface not governed as code. No change review process. No drift detection.
findings.recommendation: Define API Gateway, IAM roles, and secrets in Terraform/CDK. Establish PR-based review. Enable AWS Config for drift detection.

compensating_controls: K8s manifests are version-controlled
Manual review via PR process

findings.title: CI/CD with API Contract Testing
findings.description: No CI/CD pipeline exists. No GitHub Actions, Jenkins, CodeBuild, or any pipeline. No automated testing or breaking change detection.
findings.gap: Cannot catch API-breaking changes before production.
findings.recommendation: Establish CI/CD pipeline with API contract tests validating response schemas against OpenAPI specification.

compensating_controls: Manual testing before deployment
Pin agent tool definitions and monitor response changes

findings.title: Sandbox/Staging Environment
findings.description: No sandbox or staging environment configuration exists. No docker-compose for local testing, no seed data scripts. K8s manifests target single environment.
findings.gap: No safe environment to test agent behavior. Agents would be tested against production.
findings.recommendation: Create docker-compose.yml for local development with MongoDB container and seed data. Define k8s overlay for staging.

compensating_controls: Local MongoDB instance for manual testing
Docker container build enables isolated testing

items.summary: Resolve the machine identity BLOCKER and address all RISK-SAFETY findings. Deploy API Gateway with per-agent identity, scoped permissions, audit logging, and rate limiting.
Create OpenAPI spec, add structured errors, implement input validation, establish CI/CD pipeline, add observability instrumentation, and create staging environment.
Address remaining INFO items as capacity allows. Implement business metrics, data quality monitoring, and rate limit headers.

recommended_actions.action: Deploy API Gateway with machine identity and per-agent authentication
recommended_actions.rationale: Resolves the only BLOCKER and addresses 4 RISK-SAFETY findings simultaneously. API Gateway provides machine identity, scoped permissions, action-level auth, agent suspension, and rate limiting in a single deployment.

recommended_actions.action: Remove hardcoded credentials and integrate Secrets Manager
recommended_actions.rationale: Hardcoded API key and MongoDB URL in source code are immediate security risks. Low effort to externalize to environment variables and Secrets Manager.

recommended_actions.action: Add request logging and audit trail
recommended_actions.rationale: Zero audit trail means no forensics capability. Add structured request logging with PII-aware field filtering.

recommended_actions.action: Create OpenAPI specification and establish CI/CD pipeline
recommended_actions.rationale: Enables automated tool generation for agents and prevents silent API breakage through contract testing.
Enables debugging agent-initiated requests and detecting service degradation before agents cascade failures.
